resources.string: Optional: you can skip this and turn it on later.
Needed to be your home screen.
You can change any of this later in Android Settings, or from Setup and permissions in the menu.
Android sends the Home key to the Home app. Choose Tenseven so the Home key opens it. You can switch back at any time in Settings, Apps, Default apps.
Names and one phone number per person appear on the Hub\'s Contacts tab, and let messages from the same person in different apps group together. Read on the phone when needed; never stored or sent.
Home can show how many photos you have. Only the count is read; pictures are not copied or uploaded.

Notification access lets the Hub list conversations per person, show unread counts and send an inline reply. Message text is read on the phone, kept in memory only and dropped when you turn this off or restart. Nothing is stored or sent. Android words this as access to all notifications; Tenseven ignores everything that is not a message or an email.

Only a home screen built into the phone can see other apps\' recent tasks. Usage access lets Tenseven read which apps you used lately, so Active Frames can show a recent-apps row. App names and times only; nothing is stored or sent.

Tenseven can include a calculator with unit conversion, notes, and some classic games. Nothing is installed or downloaded and none is on by default: tick what you want and it appears in All Apps. You can change this any time from Extra apps in Command.
Choose the bundled Calculator, Notes and games

Lets Tenseven lock the screen when you double-tap empty space on Home. It cannot see or change anything on screen.
